key_insight: The paper turns supply-chain disruption recovery into an open capacity pooling problem, where ADMM coordinates incumbents and an LLM-guided search finds compatible outside capacity when exact offers are revealed.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical decision-support framework for resilient logistics networks that can discover and re-optimize spare capacity without requiring providers to share full proprietary models.
method: Use ADMM to coordinate incumbent network members without exposing their full optimization models.
Use residual capacity gaps to direct LLM-ranked searches over unstructured provider profiles.
Verify revealed offers, screen them by reduced cost, then warm-start re-optimization.
evidence_signal: Across 200 synthetic disruption episodes, the full-information version recovered 24.6% of capacity-scarcity cost, while with 40 contacts the directed LLM approach captured 32.0% of that value versus 4.7% for undirected contact.
watch_item: The method is only guaranteed optimal when every eligible offer is revealed at exact prices; performance depends on profile quality, offer disclosure, and the cost of contacting providers.
paper_title: Open Capacity Pooling in Agentic Supply Chains: Coordination-Directed LLM Discovery and Distributed Re-optimization
